agents.name: manager
agents.system_message: A human manager. They will dictate the task and test finished drafts

agents.name: planner
agents.system_message:
You and your group will be tasked with creating a python app which accomplishes the managers request. 
        Your job is the planner. When presented with a request, first try to understand what the manager is asking. Do this by explaining in more detail what the manager is asking for, and what the main challenges will be. Be specific and concise.

        Next, you should develop a plan to solve the request. Explain what will need to be done, and why, in the app. Have a logical order - this will be passed on to the programmer as a settled plan.

        Here is an example of what a settled plan would look like for a request:

        -----------

        The manager has asked us to {the managers request}.

        In other words, what the manager is asking for is {more complete request definition/explanation}

        This means, we need to {expand on functional requirements}


        A successful app for this task must achieve these things:
        1. Functionality/Feature 1
            - Guide for achieving Functionality/Feature 1 
        2. Functionality/Feature 2
            - Guide for achieving Functionality/Feature 2 
        3. Functionality/Feature 3
            - Guide for achieving Functionality/Feature 3 

        Do you agree, manager?

        ------------

        Nice and short and succicnt, while still having the necessary information. Please use this as a guide.

        Work with the manager until the manager approves of the plan. The manager will approve of the plan by using the phrase "sounds good"

        Once the manager said "sounds good", you can write a call to write_settled_plan to write the settled plan into memory. Do not alter the plan after manager approval. Simply remove the question, "Do you agree, manager?".

agents.name: programmer
agents.system_message:
You and your group will be tasked with creating a python app which accomplishes the managerss request. Your job is the coder. You will be presented with a plan consisting of the necessary features and functional components. You will produce a python script which attempts to accomplish all of the tasks. However, some tasks are harder than others, and it may be best to leave a comment about what should be there, or what needs to be done. This is an iterative process, so you can expect a chance to revisit the code to fill in the blanks. You do not need to do everything on the first try. If you believe a section of code will be too hard to figure out on the first time, please consider leaving a note that can be tackled on the next iteration.
            
            Do not participate in any conversation or dialog. Your only output should be well formatted code blocks, and nothing else. It is someone elses job to review.
            
            You are only to produce code-blocks. Do not preempt the code with any extra text, and do not add any after it.

agents.name: reviewer
agents.system_message:
You and your group will be tasked with creating a python app which accomplishes the items set out in the plan. You are the reviewer. 
        You will review the managers request, the planners interpretation of the request, the approved plan, and the latest code iteration.

        Read through the code, and explain what you see in the code. Explain what look like it should work OK, as it relates to the request and plan.

        If there are errors, the code will go through another iteration. If you believe there are errors, to help guide the programmer, explain what is not OK, and why it is not OK.

        Do not write any code. Just explain in easy to understand terms.

        Your job is critical - please be logical, focus, and try your best.

requirements.description: Planner must generate a structured project plan with functional requirements when given a user request.
expected_behavior: Planner responds with a plan containing numbered functional requirements.
Plan must include explanation of request, challenges, and a list of features/guides.
negative_cases: Planner outputs only a single line without structured plan.
Planner refuses to generate any plan.

requirements.description: Planner must save the approved plan using write_settled_plan tool when manager says 'sounds good'.
expected_behavior: When manager input contains 'sounds good', planner calls write_settled_plan.
Plan content saved to file in the project folder.
negative_cases: Planner saves plan without manager approval.
Planner modifies plan content after calling write_settled_plan.

requirements.description: Coder must output only well-formatted code blocks, no extra text.
expected_behavior: Coder message contains only a code block or multiple code blocks.
No conversational text, explanations, or summaries.
negative_cases: Coder outputs prose before or after code block.
Coder refuses to generate code because of missing context.

requirements.description: Reviewer must provide comments evaluating code against plan, without writing any code.
expected_behavior: Reviewer explains what works OK and what needs improvement in the context of the plan.
Reviewer output is pure text, no code blocks.
negative_cases: Reviewer only outputs 'looks good' without specifics.

requirements.description: Manager can execute write_latest_iteration to save Coder code to script file.
expected_behavior: When manager triggers write_latest_iteration, code content is written to a new script_v{n}.py in project folder.
negative_cases: File is saved to wrong directory.

requirements.description: Iteration loop must present latest script and comments to Coder and Reviewer.
expected_behavior: Coder receives plan + latest script + latest comments as context.
Reviewer receives plan + latest script + latest comments as context.
Only latest versions are presented, not previous iterations.
negative_cases: Old script versions are included in context.
Iteration continues after manager exit signal.

requirements.description: System must support resuming an existing project.
expected_behavior: On restart, system detects existing projects and offers continue option.
If continued, latest plan, script, and comments are loaded and an iteration starts with Coder.
negative_cases: Resume crashes if no script_v1.py exists.

requirements.description: System must handle manager feedback during iteration without moving to next agent.
expected_behavior: When manager provides feedback (not exit), the current agent revises its output.
The conversation remains on the same agent until manager types exit.
negative_cases: Manager input 'exit' is ignored and conversation continues.
Feedback results in immediate switch to next agent.

semantic_graph_review.semantic_graph_review: The semantic graph is mostly consistent with the documented agent roles. The manager initiates chats with planner, programmer, and reviewer, which matches the main loop logic. However, there are missing edges that reflect the actual runtime handoffs: planner -> manager (for approval), manager -> programmer (after approval), programmer -> reviewer (via manager-controlled loop), reviewer -> programmer (for iterative feedback), and programmer -> manager (when iteration is done). Currently only manager-initiated edges are present, which under-represents the actual communication flow. Additionally, the tool assignments are incomplete: the planner is listed without tools in the profile, but the system message and R2 clearly indicate that planner must call write_settled_plan. In the actual agent definition (IterativeTools.py line 26), planner is configured with a 'functions' list that includes write_settled_plan. This discrepancy is a semantic inconsistency. Similarly, the reviewer is not assigned any tools in the profile, but the underlying code provides write_latest_iteration_comments; however, review of the system message shows the reviewer is explicitly told not to write code, only explain, which is consistent with not having tools, so this is not a risk. The termination conditions 'TERMINATE' and 'max_turns' are standard. The profile states only manager has tools, but the evidence from requirements and code shows planner should have write_settled_plan. This mismatch can lead to test failures where planner is expected to use the tool but the tool is not registered for it in tests, resulting in tool_schema_risk.

suspected_risk_points.evidence: Profile lists planner with tools: [] (no tools). However, requirement R2 expects planner to call write_settled_plan. In the source code IterativeTools.py line 26, planner is created with a 'functions' parameter that includes write_settled_plan. This indicates the tool should be available to planner, but the profile omits it. If the test environment relies on the profile to decide tool registration, planner will not have access to write_settled_plan, causing tool call failures.

additional_edges.evidence: Planner must interact with manager to get approval ('sounds good') as per R2.
In the iteration loop (main.py), after programmer produces code, the manager initiates a chat with reviewer passing the code. This creates a logical edge.
Reviewer feedback is passed back to programmer for next iteration, as per system description and R6.
Manager triggers write_latest_iteration after programmer output, and can provide feedback directly to programmer during iteration.
